pages.text: Mobs in IridescentCraft are significantly tougher than vanilla. This is not a bug — it is a core design decision. Mobs should be $(italic)real threats$() that require you to invest in your class, gear, and combat skills.$(br2)$(thing)Base HP multipliers$() apply to all mobs by category before any other scaling.

pages.title: HP Multipliers
pages.text: $(bold)Basic mobs$() (zombies, skeletons, spiders, etc.) — $(thing)3× HP$()$(br)$(bold)Mid-tier mobs$() (endermen, witches, piglins, etc.) — $(thing)1.5× HP$()$(br)$(bold)Bosses$() (Wither, Dragon, mod bosses) — $(thing)Unchanged$()$(br2)Basic mobs receive the largest multiplier because they are the most common and should not die in one hit. Mid-tier mobs are already somewhat durable. Bosses are balanced individually and do not need blanket scaling.

pages.title: Dimension Stacking
pages.text: HP multipliers $(bold)stack with dimension scaling$(). Each dimension applies its own multiplier on top of the base toughness tier.$(br2)$(bold)Example:$() A zombie (3× base) in the Nether (4× dimension) has $(thing)12×$() its vanilla HP. That same zombie in the End would be even tougher.$(br2)This is intentional. Early-dimension mobs in late-game dimensions are not free kills — they scale to remain dangerous.

pages.title: What This Means for You
pages.text: You cannot brute-force your way through IridescentCraft with a stone sword. Invest in your $(thing)class abilities$(), upgrade your $(thing)gear$(), and use $(thing)buffs and enchantments$() to keep pace with mob scaling.$(br2)If a mob feels too tanky, you are probably undergeared for that dimension. Check the $(l:icraft:systems/dimension_mechanics)Dimension Mechanics$(/l) entry for expected power levels per zone.$(br2)$(italic)The pack rewards preparation. Rushing a dimension without proper gear is a fast way to burn through repair costs.$()
